articles.title: Aces star A'ja Wilson reportedly avoids WNBA punishment following confrontation with fan
articles.summary: The fan was removed briefly from his seat, but not ejected from the arena.
articles.body:
The WNBA reportedly will not fine or suspend A'ja Wilson after the forward confronted a fan during the Las Vegas Aces ' Game 2 loss to the Indiana Fever at Gainbridge Field house on Tuesday.

According to The Athletic's Annie Costabile and Chantel Jennings , the game officials determined Wilson was still in the court area when she approached the fan and not in the stands. That was why she did not end up getting ejected. The high-pressure situation of it being a playoff game was also a factor the league took into consideration when determining whether to dole out punishment.

Midway through the fourth quarter, Wilson was trying to fight through a screen set by Sophie Cunningham when the two got tangled up. Cunningham was sent down to the court hard and was called for a foul.

But as Wilson was walking down the lane after play had stopped, she suddenly erupted at a fan sitting behind the basket. Wilson had to be pulled back by several teammates and officials. It's unclear what was actually said by the fan to spark the exchange, but Wilson was livid.

Wilson was assessed a technical foul for unsportsmanlike conduct and could have been kicked out.

"Any coach, player, or trainer who deliberately enters the spectator stands during the game will be automatically ejected," states the WNBA rulebook . But the first row of fans is what is considered the beginning of the "spectator stands."

The fan was removed from his seat briefly, but returned soon after and was spotted celebrating with people sitting around him, according to Fever reporter Tony East .

Wilson said she apologized to her team for the technical foul, but she's not sorry for her actions.

"If I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don't give a damn what you said. I don't give a damn how you said it, the tone, that is unacceptable," Wilson said after the game. "You don't know me to step towards me and point at me. I'm not for that s*** at all. … That there is unacceptable. How he gets back in the game because they said he didn't do anything, of course he did. articles.title: A'ja Wilson Reportedly Won't Be Disciplined by WNBA for Fan Confrontation During Aces vs. Fever

articles.body:
Las Vegas Aces superstar A'ja Wilson will not face any disciplinary action from the WNBA, according to Chantel Jennings and Annie Costabile of The Athletic, after confronting a fan during a 99-89 loss to the Indiana Fever on Tuesday.

Per that report, "on-court game officials determined that Wilson was in the court area—what is known as a player escape lane—adjacent to the stanchion rather than the stands. Based on that determination, officials decided there was no cause for an ejection."

Wilson was given a technical foul, however. After the game, she said the man pointed at her and walked toward her.

"I try to play my game... but if I am just walking, just got the foul, I'm chilling and I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don't give a damn what you said," she said. "I don't give a damn how you said it, the tone. That is unacceptable. You don't step toward me. You never should sit and point at me. That there is unacceptable."

The fan was initially removed from his seat by security but was allowed to return after the Fever determined he didn't violate the Fan Code of Conduct.

"I didn't exactly see what happened," Aces' head coach Becky Hammon told reporters after the game. "I kind of saw the aftermath. I've never seen Wilson go like that. So whatever was done, I can tell you she felt very disrespected in that moment. I've never seen her really react like that, ever. So whatever it was, it doesn't have any place, I don't think, in an arena. There's rules and procedures. I think there's a certain etiquette that both players and fans need to abide by, but clearly the lines get crossed, and it seems to happen here [at Indiana]. I can't speak specifically as to what was said or what was done. But I can speak to the character of our players, and the stuff that they deal with. The disrespect—whether that's a word or an action, a gesture—should be addressed appropriately. That's not my job. It's the job of this arena. So I assume they are following protocol."

articles.title: NIT, WBIT Reveal Bracket Format, Selection Process Changes After NCAA Tournament Expansion
articles.summary: The NIT and WBIT tournaments are undergoing changes on the heels of the men's and women's NCAA basketball tournaments expanding from 68 to 76 teams.
articles.body:
The NIT and WBIT tournaments are undergoing changes on the heels of the men's and women's NCAA basketball tournaments expanding from 68 to 76 teams.

The NCAA announced Thursday that the NIT and WBIT fields will both shrink from 32 teams to 24 teams each, starting in 2027.

Both the NIT and WBIT will award the No. 1 seeds in their tournaments to the schools designated as the "First Four Out" of the men's and women's NCAA tournaments as well.

Dan Hurley Halloween decoration going viral

The NIT's selection process will see each of the top 10 conferences based on Ken Pomeroy's rankings receive an exempt bid into the tourney, plus an extra exempt bid to both the ACC and SEC.

Bids will also be awarded to regular-season conference champions that did not qualify for the NCAA tournament, provided they are ranked 125th or better when using the average of the ESPN Basketball Power Index, Ken Pomeroy Rating, Kevin Pauga Index, NCAA Evaluation Tool (NET), Strength of Record, Torvik and Wins Above Bubble (WAB) rankings.

There will be eight first-round games in the NIT with the winners of those games moving on to face the top eight seeds in the second round.

The better-seeded team will host each game at their home venue until the NIT Finals, which will be played at the University of Detroit Mercy on April 4, 2027.

As for the WBIT, teams must have a record of .500 or better to have a chance at an at-large bid, and teams with an average ranking of 100 or better in WAB and NET will be considered.

Teams that won their regular-season conference championship and have an average WAB and NET ranking of 110 or better will receive automatic entry into the WBIT.

The WBIT will have the same format as the NIT with the winners of the eight first-round games facing the eight top seeds in the second round

However, both the semifinals and finals will be held at a central location with Koch Arena in Wichita, Kansas, hosting the semis on March 29, 2027, and the finals on March 31, 2027.

The best role for LeBron James on the Philadelphia 76ers has been debated after he signed with the team this summer, though most believe he would be best-suited operating as the de facto point guard.

James is one of the best passers in NBA history and a brilliant basketball mind, often operating as a point forward and coach out on the court. He's also 41 and took a step back from being a primary scoring threat with the Los Angeles Lakers last season, letting Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves take on a heavier burden in that regard.

So operating as more of a traditional point guard would hardly be a stretch. He's already said he's willing to play whatever role is required of him:

articles.title: Napheesa Collier says she hasn't thought about free agency yet after Lynx's surprising first-round playoff exit
articles.summary: Napheesa Collier has two major decisions to make this offseason.
articles.body:
Napheesa Collier has an important decision to make this offseason. After spending her first eight seasons with the Minnesota Lynx , Collier will be an unrestricted free agent. While she's had opportunities to leave the franchise in the past, she's always returned. But after another premature playoff exit, could Collier decide to take her talents elsewhere?

The five-time All-Star hasn't entertained that question yet. Just days after the team's surprising loss to the New York Liberty , Collier said she hasn't had time to decompress and think about the future just yet.

She did, however, reiterate her love for the Lynx and the city of Minnesota, per Colin Salao of Front Office Sports.

"I haven't even thought about that. We lost less than 48 hours ago, and I don't think, we didn't expect to be here, you know. So I really haven't had any time to decompress or anything like that. "I can tell you, I love it here. I love the organization. I love it here. I love the organization. But I just haven't had the time to give it any thought."

The first-round loss clearly came as a shock to Collier. That's to be expected after the Lynx turned in a WNBA-best 33-11 record in 2026. The team accomplished that feat despite Collier playing in just 16 regular-season games after missing time with ankle injuries at the start of the season.

In those 16 games, Collier averaged 16.8 points, 6.9 rebounds and 2.6 assists.

In Collier's absence, the Lynx were buoyed by All-Stars Natasha Howard and Courtney Williams . The team also received excellent production from veteran Kayla McBride and unanimous Rookie of the Year winner Olivia Miles.

All four of those players are under contract with the team next season, giving Collier a good chance to add another championship to her résumé if she re-signs with the franchise. While Collier didn't commit to doing that Thursday, she didn't rule out the possibility, either, merely saying she still needs time to consider her future.

It's not the only big decision Collier has to make over the offseason. With long-time WNBPA president Nneka Ogwumike retiring from the WNBA , that position will be up for grabs this offseason. Collier was elected as the union's First Vice-President in June, giving her a line to the top job if she wants it.

Collier was non-committal about the position when asked Thursday, per FOS.

"That is another thing that I haven't really thought about, just because obviously you're just so focused on the season when it's happening. And I think that's something that we're going to have to talk about as a union. We haven't had any talks of an election or anything like that, so that's something I'm going to have to sit down and think about. And so I don't know what the future holds."

Though Collier's numbers were down coming off her injuries, she's still young enough to return to MVP form, especially if she has a fully healthy offseason.

Whether that comes with the Lynx or elsewhere remains to be seen, but it's probably important for Collier to carefully consider both decisions over the offseason. Each one can have a profound effect on the future of the WNBA and should not be taken lightly.

articles.title: Knicks' Josh Hart Explains Why Joint Replacement Surgery on Finger Injury Would End NBA Career
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Josh Hart expanded Thursday on his statement that he has no other option than to play with a wrapped ring finger on his right hand until he retires from the NBA.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Josh Hart expanded Thursday on his statement that he has no other option than to play with a wrapped ring finger on his right hand until he retires from the NBA.

"The only option for my finger at this point, because of how damaged it is, is a full joint replacement, and with a joint replacement... grabbing a rebound, palming it, shooting it, catching the ball, doing it all, you can't do that," Hart told reporters Thursday (h/t SNY). "So, if I did a joint replacement, then I wouldn't be able to play. So I guess it's either wrap it 'til I retire or cut it off, I guess that's the other option."

Hart added the pain level of the impacted finger, which is visibly crooked, varies from day to day.

"Some days it'll be good, some days it'll hurt to catch the ball... Some days it's good, and it's just like a regular functioning finger. Other days it hurts to just close my hand," Hart said.

Hart's interview followed a Tuesday social media post in which he said his finger would be "wrapped until I retire."

He added Thursday he plans to undergo joint replacement surgery following his eventual retirement from the NBA.

Hart dislocated his finger during Game 6 of the 2025 Eastern Conference Finals against the Indiana Pacers in July 2025. He underwent surgery on the injury later that month.

He said in September he had re-injured the finger during training camp and now expected to wear a splint until he could "try to fix it again next summer," per the AP .

Hart's injury didn't stop him from shooting 41.3 percent from behind the arc during the regular season before firing 32.6 percent from deep during the Knicks' run to the 2026 title.

Knicks coach Mike Brown said he was impressed by Hart's toughness but not by the aesthetics of the injured finger.

"Josh is a handsome young man, but that finger is ugly," Brown said (h/t Kristian Winfield of the New York Daily News) . "It adds to his toughness. I can't even imagine having a finger like that."

Hart himself admitted , "It's not the prettiest to look at. I would love to have a straight finger. But it works."

The Knicks will hope Hart's eventual joint replacement surgery won't be coming in the immediate future. The 31-year-old is signed through this season with a team option for 2027-28, and he's a key part of the Knicks' hopes of running things back with the majority of last season's title-winning roster.

That push will start Oct. 20 when the Knicks tip off the season with a game against LeBron James and the visiting Philadelphia 76ers.

articles.title: Angel Reese Wins 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year Award, Full Voting Results Announced
articles.summary: One day after helping the Atlanta Dream win their first playoff series in eight years, Angel Reese has been named WNBA Defensive Player of the Year for the 2026 season.
articles.body:
One day after helping the Atlanta Dream win their first playoff series in eight years, Angel Reese has been named WNBA Defensive Player of the Year for the 2026 season.

The WNBA announced the voting results for the award on Thursday with Reese receiving 46 out of 74 votes, beating out Gabby Williams (20 votes), A'ja Wilson (four votes), Shakira Austin (two votes), Veronica Burton (one vote) and Rhyne Howard (one vote).

Reese reacted to the honor by posting a video on social media:

Reese joined the Dream in the offseason after being acquired in a trade with the Chicago Sky for two first-round draft picks. She responded to the change of scenery with arguably the best season of her career.

The 24-year-old was one of two players to average a double-double in the regular season, along with Dallas Wings forward Jessica Shepard. She set career-highs in scoring average (16.4 points) and steals (1.8) in 43 starts.

Reese ranked in the top four of all players this season in defensive rating (100.0), defensive rebound percentage (30.3) and total defensive rebounds (315). She led the league in defensive win shares (3.4).

Atlanta finished second in defensive rating and fifth in points allowed per game during the regular season. The Minnesota Lynx, Golden State Valkyries and Washington Mystics were the only other teams in the top five in both categories.

Reese is the first Dream player to be named Defensive Player of the Year. She's also the first player from an Eastern Conference club to win the award since Sylvia Fowles with the Sky in 2013.

The Dream had the best record in the Eastern Conference and tied the franchise record with 30 regular-season wins. They swept the Mystics in the first round of the playoffs to reach the semifinals for the first time since the current playoff format was adopted in 2022.

articles.title: Angel Reese wins WNBA's 2026 Defensive Player of the Year award after first season with Dream
articles.summary: Angel Reese led the league in rebounding with the Dream.
articles.body:
Angel Reese proved to be everything the Atlanta Dream needed and more in her first season with the franchise. Now, she has the hardware to prove it.

Reese won the WNBA's Defensive Player of the Year award Thursday, the league announced. She received 46 of 74 votes for the honor.

Gabby Williams finished as the runner-up behind Reese, picking up 20 votes. Three-time Defensive Player of the Year winner A'ja Wilson finished third, taking home four votes.

While Reese has developed a reputation as one of best rebounders the game has ever seen — leading the league in the stat in each of her three seasons — that hasn't led to defensive recognition until 2026. Despite her excellence on the glass, Reese has never been named to a WNBA All-Defensive team or received votes for Defensive Player of the Year prior to this season.

Rebounds, unsurprisingly, played a role in Reese finally achieving the honor this season, as she once again led the WNBA with 12.3 rebounds per game. She also set two records, pulling down the most rebounds in a single season (521) and the most offensive rebounds in a single season (206). She also set the single-game rebound record after pulling down 26 during an August game against the Los Angeles Sparks .

Her success went beyond that, though, as the WNBA highlighted in its release announcing Reese's win.

Reese's impact was evident across every defensive measure. She finished the regular season first in the WNBA in Defensive Win Shares (3.39) and fourth in defensive rating (100.0), while Atlanta allowed 7.9 fewer points per 100 possessions with Reese on the floor, the largest defensive on/off differential among Dream rotation players.

With the win, Reese also becomes the first player in Dream history to take home the award.

Reese's on-court contributions were a significant reason the Dream once again posted one of the best records in the WNBA. With the regular season done — and an award already in hand — Reese will now see if she can add a championship ring to her collection.

articles.title: Un Real Madrid bipolar remonta 22 puntos pero no evita el peor inicio de su historia en Europa
articles.standfirst: Los blancos perdían 67-45 tras una primera mitad fantasmagórica, se levantaron con TLC, Maledon y Tavares (74-75) y acabaron cayendo a manos de Bryant para colocarse 0-3
articles.summary: Los blancos perdían 67-45 tras una primera mitad fantasmagórica, se levantaron con TLC, Maledon y Tavares (74-75) y acabaron cayendo a manos de Bryant para colocarse 0-3
articles.body: Un Real Madrid bipolar hizo lo más difícil, levantar 22 puntos al Hapoel Tel Aviv, para acabar cediendo por 102-98 en la tercera derrota consecutiva para empezar la Euroliga. Un lastre ese 0-3 que puede arrastrar durante la temporada y también el peor inicio de su historia en competiciones europeas. No bastó una remontada exprés. Tampoco las grandes actuaciones de Maledon (26 puntos y siete asistencias para 40 de valoración) y Tavares (14+13). Ni el bestial tercer cuarto de Luwawu-Cabarrot (14 puntos con cuatro triples). Las alarmas ya están encendidas. Suerte que el conjunto blanco ganó la SuperCup, aunque aquello parece un espejismo viendo el presente. Los madridistas, tras una primera parte fantasmagórica (63-43), se vieron 67-45 al inicio de la segunda. En una mutación liderada por Maledon y Luwawu-Cabarrot, consiguieron remontar en sólo siete minutos con un parcial de 7-30 que incluyó un 0-19. El 74-75 fue su única ventaja en toda la tarde. Pero después de tanto remar, el Madrid no consiguió alcanzar la orilla. Los errores volvieron a condenarle y un extraordinario Elijah Bryant se adueñó del último cuarto. Hizo lo que quiso y liquidó rozando el triple-doble: 22 puntos, 13 rebotes y siete asistencias para 40 de valoración. Los blancos pasaron de la nada, al infinito y de ahí a la decepción. Y a la preocupación. En la primera mitad, el Madrid fue un grupo de espectros cuya defensa el Hapoel atravesó sin problemas. Caboclo castigó a Tavares con triples y Leday, que hizo 13 puntos en el primer cuarto, tiró de versatilidad para comerse a Pradilla en dos minutos. A los siete, Pedro Martínez ya había hecho jugar a sus 12 efectivos, pero seguía sin dar con la tecla. Smith pagaba la novatada con las faltas y sólo Okeke tuvo algo de puntería entre ataques deslavazados jugados muy lejos del aro. Al final del primer cuarto, 29-20. Iría a mucho peor. Porque Micic, a cero hasta entonces, tomó el mando. Encontró una autopista hacia el aro y sumó 14 puntos en el segundo acto. Tanto él como Oturu y Satoransky se colgaron del aro aprovechando los pasillos y Caboclo hizo dos triples más. Por dentro y por fuera, el Hapoel destrozaba a un Madrid cuya defensa rozaba lo ridículo: 54-34 a falta de tres minutos para el descanso. Al intermedio se llegó con 63-43 después de que Campazzo fallara una entrada solo. Buena metáfora de lo visto hasta entonces. No salía nada. Tampoco de inicio, pues Leday ponía la máxima (67-45). Pero cuando más muerto parecía el Madrid, se levantó. Un par de buenas defensas le permitieron correr por primera vez. A TLC se le calentó la mano para meter cuatro triples y Maledon puso el criterio en la dirección. Al Hapoel se le hizo de noche. Estuvo cuatro minutos sin anotar. Lo que antes metía ahora se le salía. El contundente parcial de 0-19 revivió al Madrid, que primero igualó a 70 y después consumó la remontada con un mate de Tavares a la contra: 74-75. Pedro Martínez había reducido las rotaciones al extremo. El quinteto formado por Maledon, Smith, TLC, Jantunen y Tavares estuvo en pista nueve minutos seguidos. Con empate a 75 se llegó al último acto. Ese le perteneció a Bryant. De su mano, el Hapoel se fue escapando. El juego se había ralentizado y el suflé del Madrid se vino abajo. Un grave error defensivo de Smith dejó a Micic solo para un triple. Una falta en ataque del último fichaje blanco la castigó Bryant para cerrar un parcial de 14-3 que volvía a poner el partido muy cuesta arriba (89-78). Su duelo final con Maledon fue épico, pero cayó del lado local. Los blancos desperdiciaron tres ataques seguidos. En uno pudo haber falta sobre Luwawu-Cabarrot, pero se acabó pitando al revés. Con 99-94 y 38 segundos por jugarse, no se hizo falta. Blakeney consiguió un 2+1 que ya sería definitivo pese al rosario de tiempos muertos pensando ya en el average. El Madrid, tras su enésimo tropiezo a domicilio, arranca 0-3. Lo nunca visto. 102 - Hapoel Tel Aviv (29+34+12+27): Micic (22), Satoransky (9), Bryant (22), LeDay (15) y Caboclo (15) -cinco inicial-, Blakeney (12), Carrington (-), Wainright (-), Odiase (-) y Oturu (7) 98 - Real Madrid (20+23+32+23): Campazzo (3), Maledon (26), Luwawu-Cabarrot (21), Jantunen (7) y Tavares (14) -cinco inicial-, Smith Jr (12), Pradilla (-), Abalde (2), Okeke (8), Deck (1), Feliz (2) y Jones (2). Eliminaron por faltas a Bruno Caboclo (min.35), del Hapoel, y a Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot (min.40), del Real Madrid. articles.title: Raptors' Kawhi Leonard hints at potential retirement timeline after extension with Toronto
articles.summary: Kawhi Leonard is back with the Toronto Raptors for his second stint with them. During his media availability, he may have let it be known around the time he...
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors are back to wanting to be serious contenders in the Eastern Conference, making it a goal to improve the roster this summer. After going through a lot of trouble, they were finally able to get their main target.

The Raptors made a trade for Kawhi Leonard , but it was put on hold due to an investigation. Finally, the trade was able to go through once the investigation concluded.

"The trade sending Kawhi Leonard from the LA Clippers to Toronto has been made official after a monthslong delay due to the NBA's investigation into the Clippers for salary cap circumvention. The teams initially agreed to the deal on June 30, but it was paused while the league investigated allegations the Clippers violated salary cap rules in signing Leonard as a free agent," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

Getting Leonard was a huge step in the right direction. Both sides are locked into each other so much that the two-time NBA champion was already given an extension.

" Toronto Raptors All-NBA star Kawhi Leonard has agreed on a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a player option for the 2028-29 season, his agent Harrison Gaines of SLASH Sports tells ESPN," Charania posted.

Leonard is likely going to be in Toronto for the rest of his career. The NBA champion has made it known that he is with the Raptors because he believes it is the best fit for his family. While answering a question on Wednesday, he hinted at a potential retirement timeline.

"Probably being four or five years away from walking away, I just want to show people who I really am, because you get so many narratives out there. People don't know me. I'm just having fun with it," Leonard said.

With this timeline, it would mean that he has one more contract left in him, as his current one with Toronto is only three years. That could be just a rough approximation, though, as he could very well retire after his current contract is up.

The Raptors know that they only have a short amount of time with Leonard, so it will be crucial to compete now. It is sad that so many beloved stars in the NBA are getting so close to retirement.

articles.title: Would Wembanyama ever endorse FanDuel or Polymarket? Don't bet on it
articles.summary: In a stance that puts him at odds with other NBA stars, the Spurs' Victor Wembanyama says he would never lend his name to a sports betting site
articles.body:
Through his first three NBA seasons, Spurs star Victor Wembanyama has signed endorsement deals with shoe companies, sports drink makers, luxury fashion brands and video-game publishers.

There is one kind of company Wembanyama vows will never get his name -- sports gambling and prediction-market sites.

Asked after Thursday's practice whether he would ever consider partnering with one - as some of his NBA counterparts have - Wembanyama was emphatic.

"Absolutely not," Wembanyama said. "I will never do that."

That stance puts Wembanyama at odds with some of the biggest names in the NBA.

Milwaukee 's Giannis Antetokounmpo is a shareholder in Kalshi, a prediction-market app. Houston 's Kevin Durant is a paid spokesman for FanDuel. Philadelphia 's LeBron James , the NBA's all-time leading scorer, recently signed a $15 million endorsement deal with Polymarket.

Without singling out any player by name, the 22-year-old Wembanyama made clear what he thinks of those choices.

"Honestly, I think it's very sad to see some players promote it," Wembanyama said.

Under league rules, players are permitted to endorse betting and prediction-market sites, provided the endorsements do not involve bets on specific NBA games or entities.

Wembanyama's portfolio includes Nike, Louis Vuitton, 2K Sports, sports-apparel company Fanatics and Barcode, a sports hydration beverage.

Like scores of Spurs stars - and non-stars - before him, he also willingly appears in locally loved H-E-B commercials each season.

But when it comes to choosing which brands to promote, Wembanyama said money is no longer the deciding factor.

"There was a dimension of money in the past. Not anymore," Wembanyama said. "Even as I say that, I've refused much, much more money for things that were not to my values."

Sticking to his principles, Wembanyama said, matters more.

"I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence in the world," Wembanyama said. "Obviously we earn millions and millions, but that is not our biggest strength. Our biggest strength is inspiring and we can inspire in a good or a bad way. I want to inspire in a good way."

For Wembanyama, at least, the Kalshi odds of ever signing with a sports gambling or prediction-market site are 0 percent.

"Everyone does whatever they want," Wembanyama said, "but without me."

articles.title: NIT and WBIT format changes along with tournament final sites announced
articles.summary: The NIT heads to Detroit, while the WBIT returns to Wichita
articles.body:
Both the NIT and WBIT announced some slight changes for their 2027 tournaments. The NCAA has also announced that the NIT championship game will be hosted at Detroit Mercy on April 4, running alongside the NCAA Tournament's Final Four, while the WBIT semifinals and championship will be held in Wichita, Kan., on March 29 and 31. Both tournaments will feature 24 teams, down from 32 because of the expansion of March Madness.

The changes to the NIT can potentially have huge implications on this year's tournament. Previously, the premiere 12 conferences would receive exempt bids for the tournament. Exempt bids are guaranteed bids to specific high achieving teams that barely missed the NCAA Tournament in said conferences. Now, exempt bids are given to the top 10 conferences. The highest ranked team in each of those conferences will automatically be included in the NIT, if accepted. Additionally, the ACC and SEC will receive one exempt bid. Conferences are ranked by the NCAA directly from Ken Pomeroy, better well-known as KenPom, who mathematically ranks every single Division-I program in the country.

The WBIT saw some changes from previous years. The first round features eight games at a hosting campus. From there, the winners will be scattered around to face the top eight seeds in the WBIT. With how teams are selected is where the huge changes came. To be considered for an at-large bit, teams must have at least a .500 regular season record. After that, teams with an average NET and WAB ranking of under 100 will be considered. Lastly, programs that won their conference regular season that have an average NET and WAB ranking 110 or better will automatically qualify for the WBIT.

With said changes to each tournament, it'll be exciting to see how each tournament looks heading into and throughout the season. Each field will be selected on Sunday, March 14 and all games will take place on ESPN Networks.

articles.title: Duke basketball lands 2027 commitment from Australian guard Luke Paul
articles.summary: Duke basketball landed its first 2027 commitment, as 6-foot-6 Australian guard Luke Paul committed to Jon Scheyer and the Blue Devils.
articles.body:
Duke basketball has landed its first commitment in its 2027 recruiting class.

Luke Paul, a 6-foot-6 point guard from Western Australia, announced his commitment to coach Jon Scheyer and the Blue Devils on Thursday, Oct. 1. Paul announced the news on ESPN's NBA Today.

"I want to go to a place that's going to help me develop my play and performance and get me to the next level which is the NBA," Paul said before unveiling his Duke shirt.

Paul will join Duke for the 2027-28 season. He is currently rostered for the Cairns Taipans of Australia's National Basketball League, signing with the club in June as part of a multi-year deal with the NBL's Next Stars program. He became the youngest player to join the program in January at 16 years old.

Paul earned MVP and All-Star Five honors at the 2025 FIBA U16 Asia Cup while helping Australia win the gold medal. He recorded 26 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists in the championship game against China and averaged 14.8 points, 7.3 rebounds and 6.3 assists throughout the tournament.

Most recently, Paul averaged 15.3 points, 6.4 rebounds and 7.1 assists at the 2026 FIBA U17 World Cup in Turkey. He was named to the tournament's All-Star Five as he led Australia to the bronze medal.

Paul's commitment gives Scheyer and the Blue Devils an early addition to their 2027 recruiting class as Duke prepares for the 2026-27 college basketball season.

Duke will officially open its season Nov. 2 against Army at Cameron Indoor Stadium. The Blue Devils are scheduled to host Countdown to Craziness on Oct. 3 and play exhibition games against Belmont, Tennessee and Kansas before the season opener.
